name: Buddhism
big_question: How do the teachings of the Buddha help Buddhists escape suffering?

glossary.d: the old man, sick man, dead man and holy man Siddhartha saw
deep concentration and reflection to develop awareness
the four main teachings of the Buddha about suffering
the belief that life involves suffering
the set of guidelines that ends suffering
to live with balance and moderation
the Buddhist festival that celebrates the birth of the Buddha
pouring water over a Buddha statue to purify heart and mind
the cycle of life, death and rebirth
the act of achieving enlightenment and escaping samsara
the consequences in the future of your actions today

lessons.title: Siddhartha Gautama
lessons.big_question: How did Siddhartha Gautama become the Buddha?
aims: DESCRIBE — who Siddhartha Gautama was
DISCUSS — why the Four Sights changed his life
EXPLAIN — what the Buddha taught about suffering

questions: What does monotheism mean?
What does polytheism mean? Which religion is polytheistic?
What is reincarnation? What is moksha?

learn.caption: The life of the Buddha, from prince to teacher
rows: The Four Sights - what he saw at 29

source.quote: He came across a holy fig tree and sat underneath it to meditate. He stayed there for 46 days, paying no attention to what was happening around him.
source.attrib: — Unit 3 lesson slides, on becoming the Buddha
source.task: Underline the words that show how hard Siddhartha worked. Why did he need to sit for so long?

stretch.question: Explain two things Siddhartha Gautama saw that changed his life.

debate.statement: You have to give up everything you own to find the meaning of life
agree: Siddhartha only found his answer after he left his palace, his riches and his family.
He taught that suffering comes because we always want more things.
disagree: Siddhartha tried living with almost nothing with the monks and only became ill, not wiser.
He later taught balance and moderation, which does not mean giving up all you own.
debate.how_to_win: Use the story of the monks. Say what Siddhartha tried, what went wrong, and what he chose instead.

quickfire.q: What is the meaning of samsara?
What are the four noble truths?

lessons.title: Wesak
lessons.big_question: Why is Wesak the most important festival in Buddhism?
aims: DESCRIBE — what happens at the festival of Wesak
DISCUSS — why religious festivals matter to believers
EXPLAIN — what the Bathing of the Buddha means

questions: Do you celebrate a religious festival? If so, how do you celebrate it?
How many religious festivals can you name?
Why do you think festivals bring people together?

learn.caption: Wesak: the festival of the Buddha's birth
rows: Bathing of the Buddha - water poured
Purify - to clean the heart and mind

source.quote: Religious festivals are a celebration of faith and togetherness. On these days, followers of a religion stand tall, united, and proud in their spirituality.
source.attrib: — Unit 3 lesson slides, on religious festivals
source.task: Pick out the three words that describe how believers feel. Which one matters most, and why?

stretch.question: Explain two ways Buddhists celebrate Wesak.

debate.statement: Wesak is the most important festival in Buddhism
agree: Wesak celebrates the birth of the Buddha, and without him there would be no Buddhism.
It is the one day when Buddhists everywhere stand together, united and proud.
disagree: The Buddha taught that meditation matters, and Buddhists meditate every day of the year.
Buddhists can purify their heart and mind at any time, not only when they bathe a statue.
debate.how_to_win: Say what Wesak celebrates, then say what Buddhists do the rest of the year. Compare the two.

quickfire.q: How long did the Buddha meditate for?
What is the Bathing of the Buddha?

lessons.title: The Vihara
lessons.big_question: What is the Vihara and why is it important to Buddhists?
aims: DESCRIBE — what a Vihara is
DISCUSS — if worship is better at home or a temple
EXPLAIN — why meditation is important to Buddhists

questions: Is it more important to pray at home or in a place of worship? Why?
Name one place of worship you have studied and one thing done there.
What might help a person concentrate when they worship?

learn.caption: Inside the Vihara: worship, study and community
rows: Worship at home or at the temple

source.quote: Meditation is a central form of worship within Buddhism. It helps control the mind, which enables you to become more aware of yourself and those around you.
source.attrib: — Unit 3 lesson slides, on worship in the Vihara
source.task: Circle the two things meditation helps a Buddhist do. Why might that make worship easier?

stretch.question: Explain two ways a Vihara is important to Buddhists.
starters: Firstly, the Vihara is important because
Secondly, the Vihara is important because

debate.statement: Buddhists do not need a Vihara because they can worship at home
agree: Buddhists can worship at home, so a temple is not needed to meditate or chant.
Meditation only needs a quiet mind, and a person can find that anywhere.
disagree: The Vihara supports the members of the community in their spiritual growth.
It is the place where Buddhists can study the religion and learn from others.
debate.how_to_win: Give both reasons the Vihara matters, then say what a home cannot give a Buddhist.

quickfire.q: What is the Bathing of the Buddha?
What is the purpose of meditation?

lessons.title: Formative assessment
lessons.big_question: How well do you know the Buddha, Wesak and the Vihara?
aims: DESCRIBE — the key words from the first three lessons
DISCUSS — which answers you found hardest and why
EXPLAIN — two Buddhist teachings in full sentences

questions: Who founded Buddhism, and what does the word Buddha mean?
What are the Four Sights that Siddhartha saw?
Name two things Buddhists do inside a Vihara.

learn.caption: Topics the formative test covers
rows: Wesak and the Bathing of the Buddha

source.quote: Firstly, one Buddhist teaching is the Bathing of the Buddha. This means that the Buddha is washed with water to purify people's hearts.
source.task: Find the point and the develop sentence. Now write a second point about the noble truths.

debate.statement: Tests are the best way to find out what you have learned
agree: A test shows exactly which key words you know and which ones you still need to revise.
Writing an answer on your own proves you can remember without any help.
disagree: A test only checks what you can recall on one day, not what you understand.
Explaining an idea to someone else can show your understanding better than a test can.
debate.how_to_win: Give one thing a test measures well and one thing it misses, then say which matters more.

lessons.title: Belief in the afterlife
lessons.big_question: What do Buddhists believe happens after death?
aims: DESCRIBE — what Buddhists believe about samsara
DISCUSS — why Buddhists want to reach Nirvana
EXPLAIN — two of the Four Noble Truths

questions: Money buys happiness. Do you agree or disagree? Why?
Name one thing you want. Would having it make you happy for ever?
What did Siddhartha say causes suffering?

learn.caption: The Four Noble Truths and life after death
rows: Samsara - cycle of death and rebirth

source.quote: Buddhists believe in life after death because the Buddha taught that human beings are each born an infinite number of times unless they achieve Nirvana.
source.attrib: — Unit 3 lesson slides, on life after death
source.task: Nirvana means escaping samsara. Explain in your own words why a Buddhist would want that.

stretch.question: Explain two of the Four Noble Truths. (4 marks)

debate.statement: It is better to live once than to be reborn again and again
agree: Buddhists say samsara is a cycle to escape from, so being reborn is not a reward.
Every new life brings dukkha, which means more suffering each time you are born.
disagree: Being born many times gives you more chances to end your desires and reach Nirvana.
Karma means your actions today shape your next life, so rebirth can be a fresh start.
debate.how_to_win: Say what samsara is, then say what Nirvana is. Judge which one a Buddhist would choose.

quickfire.q: What does the word Buddha mean?

lessons.title: Buddhism and nature
lessons.big_question: What responsibility do Buddhists have to protect the environment?
aims: DESCRIBE — sentient and non-sentient beings
DISCUSS — whether materialism harms the planet
EXPLAIN — how the Middle Way guides Buddhists

questions: We will not be alive to see the future, so why look after the environment?
Give one reason to agree and one reason to disagree.
Name two things people do that harm the environment.

learn.caption: Buddhists, nature and living with balance
rows: Care for all life, avoid causing harm

source.quote: The Buddha did not teach specifically about climate change, but he taught that Buddhists should care for all living things and avoid causing harm.
source.attrib: — Unit 3 lesson slides, on the Buddha's way of life
source.task: The Buddha never mentioned climate change. Explain how his teaching still applies today.

stretch.question: How does the Middle Way teach Buddhists to treat the environment?

debate.statement: Buying the newest phone every year is wrong for a Buddhist
agree: Buying things to impress others is materialism, and desire is what causes suffering.
Making new phones can destroy habitats, and Buddhists are taught not to harm nature.
disagree: The Middle Way means balance, not going without, so owning a phone is not wrong.
It is the reason for buying that matters, not the object a Buddhist owns.
debate.how_to_win: Use the words materialism and Middle Way. Say when buying is greed and when it is balance.

quickfire.q: Name one Hindu belief about nature.
How many noble truths are there?
What is a way to get rid of suffering?

lessons.title: Summative assessment
lessons.big_question: Can you explain what Buddhists believe and why it matters?
aims: DESCRIBE — the key words from the whole unit
DISCUSS — which topic you need to revise most
EXPLAIN — two noble truths using point and develop

questions: Write down every key word you can remember from this unit.
Which two topics do you feel least sure about? Why?
In three lines, explain the story of the Buddha.

learn.caption: Topics the summative test covers
rows: Key words: ten definitions to match
The four noble truths: explain two
Nirvana: why Buddhists want to reach it

source.quote: Firstly, there is Dukkha. This means that life involves suffering. Secondly, there is Nirodha. This means that suffering can be ended.
source.task: Each point has a develop sentence. Add one more sentence to each to make it stronger.

stretch.question: Explain two reasons why Buddhists want to reach Nirvana.

debate.statement: Buddhism is a religion even though it has no God
agree: Buddhists have a holy book, festivals, temples and beliefs about life after death.
They follow the teachings of the Buddha as an example of how to live a good life.
disagree: Buddhism is neither monotheistic nor polytheistic, so there is no God to worship.
It is based on the teachings of a man, which makes it more like a way of life.
debate.how_to_win: Say what other religions have that Buddhism has too, then say what it does not have.
